newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Q3 GDP seen having grown 2.4 pct - EconMin.
newsitem.headline: Spain Q3 GDP seen having grown 2.4 pct - EconMin.

text.p: Spain's Economy Ministry estimated on Thursday that economic activity in the third quarter grew 2.4 percent over the prior-year quarter or three percent over the previous quarter.

"One can assume that Spanish third quarter growth was significantly above the average of the first half of the year. The rate could be set at three percent annualised over the prior quarter or 2.4 percent over the year-ago quarter," according to the Ministry's latest report.
These provisional estimates are based on a synthetic indicator of activity created by the Ministry and other sources.
According to this indicator, and excluding the agricultural sector, economic activity would have grown at a 3.1 percent annualised rate in the third quarter.
Recently, Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said Spain had grown at a rate of 3.1 percent without specifying to which indicator he was referring.

For the fourth quarter, data points "to continuing expansion, with year-on-year growth of about 2.8 percent. With this, average annual growth in 1996 would reach the 2.3 percent rate forecast," the report said.
The recovery in activity would be supported by more dynamic investment in capital goods, private consumption and exports.
On the other hand, the report repeated that private consumption was recoverying albeit "moderately and unevenly according to the type of expenditure."
